trigger_condition: On Windows, HOME is not the standard environment variable for the user home directory (USERPROFILE is); in a clean Windows environment without HOME set, config_path() returns '/.codemie/codemie-cli.config.json'
guard_snippet: #[cfg(windows)] let home = std::env::var("USERPROFILE").or_else(|_| std::env::var("HOME")).unwrap_or_default(); — with a unit test that calls read_codemie_config() after writing a temp config file to the resolved path
potential_consequence: On Windows without HOME set (e.g. Windows Sandbox, stock Windows without Git for Windows), std::fs::read_to_string('/.codemie/codemie-cli.config.json') returns Err, so read_codemie_config() returns CodemieConfig::default() (state=no-configuration). renderIdentity shows 'CodeMie Desktop' instead of the user's account/profile even when a valid ~/.codemie/codemie-cli.config.json exists. The codemie_config.rs tests only call parse_config() with hardcoded strings and never exercise config_path() or the file-read path.
consumer: renderer.js:800 via bridge.codemieConfig.read() → invoke('read_codemie_config') → config_path() → std::fs::read_to_string
evidence: Read codemie_config.rs:326: fn config_path() { let home = std::env::var("HOME").unwrap_or_default(); format!("{home}/.codemie/...") } — no #[cfg(windows)] branch. The five tests in the module (unreadable_file_is_no_configuration, resolving_active_profile_is_valid, valid_config_may_record_no_account, unresolvable_active_profile_is_broken_but_still_readable, state_serializes_to_its_documented_name) all call parse_config(raw_string) directly — none call config_path() or read_codemie_config(). docs/testing/codemie-sandbox-smoke.ps1 does not set HOME and does not assert identity bar content.
